rationale: Reduplicated noun for intense sensual desire. Used four times on this page (lines 1, 4) in direct parallel with Greek ⲉⲡⲓⲑⲩⲙⲓⲁ (lines 3, 4). The doubled root carries the connotation of agitated, burning desire. Cognate qualitative ⲗⲉϩⲗⲁϩⲧ 'desirable, lust-arousing' (line 7).

Qualitative form of the same root as ⲡⲗⲁϩⲗⲉϩ. Modifies the icon (line 7): 'the icon there which is desire-arousing and beautiful (ⲛⲉⲥⲱⲥ).' Captures the active power the icon exerts upon the archons who behold it.

Standard Coptic ϣⲓⲃⲉ 'change' substantivized. Three occurrences on this page (lines 5, 7 [verb], 13). In line 5 'change of pleasure' (= sexual reciprocity); in line 13 'changes of this icon' = the cosmic alterations of the divine icon's likeness in worldly registers.
Lycopolitan compound likely from ⲡⲉϥ-ⲥϩⲓⲙⲉ 'his woman/wife' with metathesis. Names the female counterpart of the male archon in the seduction-of-archons myth that produces Adam and Eve.

Apparent scribal/dialectal variant of Greek πέρας (cf. ⲡⲡⲓⲣⲁⲥ ⲛ̄ⲑⲁⲗⲁⲥⲥⲁ in glossary). The construction ⲡⲣⲓⲅⲁⲥ ⲛ̄ⲑⲁⲗⲁⲥⲥⲁ matches the cosmological motif of the Father of Life setting the sea's bound (cf. Job 38:8-11).

ⲭⲡⲟ = Lyc. for ϫⲡⲟ 'beget' + Greek συνουσία 'sexual union, intercourse.' Standard Manichaean term contrasting natural human procreation with the special primordial molding of certain figures (line 21-22).
Lycopolitan variant of ⲛⲁⲓ̈- 'these.' Found in ⲁⲓ̈ⲡⲗⲁⲥⲙⲁ ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ 'all these moldings' (line 20), opening a new section after the leer-break. Distinct from perfect-prefix homograph.
Lyc. extended form of ⲟⲩⲱϩ 'place, set' with prosthetic ϣ-. Used here of the Father setting the boundary in the sea (line 25).
